nodes.description: A naturally occurring 1-bp insertion in a guanine run in exon 4 of canine MPV17 shifts the frame and truncates the protein. Homozygous dogs have about half the MPV17 mRNA in blood, and the truncated protein was not detected when expressed in cells. Despite this, owner-reported health records showed no enrichment of any disease in homozygous dogs, which were reported to live normal lives; mtDNA copy number in blood was inconclusive and liver and muscle were not studied.

nodes.description: Mitochondrial dGTP and dTTP fall in tissues that depend on mtDNA replication with little de novo supply, most clearly in liver and in quiescent cells. The direct evidence is the measured pool deficit and its correction by deoxynucleoside supplementation; MPV17 has not been shown to transport a deoxynucleotide. A cell study also linked MPV17 loss to low mitochondrial folate and to uracil in mtDNA, consistent with poor thymidylate supply.

nodes.description: Saccharomyces cerevisiae lacking SYM1, the MPV17 orthologue, or carrying SYM1 alleles equivalent to human missense variants. The strains lose respiratory growth under stress and form petite colonies (large mtDNA deletions or depletion), and sym1-null mitochondria have reduced levels of all four dNTPs. Most missense proteins reach mitochondria but fail to join the high molecular weight complex. A repurposing screen found ten approved drugs that raise the mitochondrial dTTP pool and reduce mtDNA instability in the yeast; none has been tested in patient cells or animals.
